skill.name: lark-vc-agent
skill.description: Guides live Lark and Feishu video meeting agent workflows. It helps a bot join active meetings, read visible events, send in-meeting messages or reactions, and leave when requested.
skill.summary: Operate a Lark meeting agent for live meeting events and controlled in-meeting actions.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Static alerts are documentation-related false positives from Markdown links, command examples, URLs, and readable non-English content. I found no prompt injection, hidden payload, or executable malware pattern in the reviewed files. The meaningful risks are consent-sensitive live meeting access and user-visible write actions, which require explicit intent and tenant permissions.

remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit user confirmation before bot join or live event reading, and preserve identity source for every meeting_id.
Require explicit user intent before sending text, sending reactions, or leaving. Use dry-run guidance when meeting identity is ambiguous.
Clarify that command blocks are examples and that user-provided text should be passed as arguments, not interpolated into shell strings.

content.value_statement: Live meeting assistants need safe access to current Lark meeting state and messages. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Lark VC agent commands for joining, reading events, sending messages, and leaving.
actual_capabilities: Join an active Lark meeting as an application bot by 9-digit meeting number.
List active meetings for the current user or a target user visible to the bot.
Read visible live meeting events, including joins, leaves, chat, transcripts, and shared documents.
Send in-meeting text messages or approved reaction emoji.
Leave a meeting by long meeting_id when the user asks.
Route post-meeting records, transcripts, and recordings to related Lark skills.
limitations: It requires lark-cli authentication, tenant installation, scopes, and VC Agent availability.
It cannot search old meetings, recordings, minutes, or participant snapshots by itself.
Bot actions are visible to meeting participants and may change live meeting state.
Application identity can only access meetings where the bot is present or permitted.

use_cases.title: Monitor a Live Project Meeting
use_cases.description: Find the current meeting, read recent visible events, and summarize active discussion points.

use_cases.title: Run a Meeting Bot Session
use_cases.description: Join a meeting with an application bot, watch live events, and leave only when asked.

use_cases.title: Send In-Meeting Feedback
use_cases.description: Send a short text message or approved reaction emoji inside an active meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Find My Current Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the active Lark meeting I am currently in and show the available meeting choices before reading events.

prompt_templates.title: Read Live Meeting Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the same identity that discovered this meeting_id and read the latest visible meeting events with pagination handled.

prompt_templates.title: Join as Meeting Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Join this 9-digit meeting number as the application bot, record the returned meeting_id, then read visible events.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Meeting Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the active meeting, confirm identity, read current events, send the requested reaction, and leave only after explicit approval.

output_examples.input: What is happening in my current meeting?
output_examples.output: The current meeting has one recent join event, two chat messages, and one shared document. The summary is based on the latest visible event pull.

output_examples.input: Send a thumbs-up in the meeting.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the active meeting, selects the approved thumbs-up reaction, and reports that the reaction was sent.

output_examples.input: Have the bot leave the meeting now.
output_examples.output: The assistant uses the recorded long meeting_id and confirms that the application bot left the meeting.

best_practices: Confirm the meeting identity and source identity before any join, send, or leave action.
Use full pagination for live event reads unless the user explicitly asks for one page.
Explain when summaries are based only on events because shared document content was unavailable.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a 9-digit meeting number as permission to join the meeting.
Do not reuse old event results when the user asks about the current meeting state.
Do not send group chat messages through this skill; route those requests to the messaging skill.

faq.question: Can this skill join a meeting automatically?
faq.answer: It should join only when the user clearly asks for a bot to enter the active meeting.

faq.question: Can it read ended meeting records?
faq.answer: No. It is for live meeting events. Ended meeting records belong to related Lark VC skills.

faq.question: Does it support user and bot identities?
faq.answer: Yes. It tracks whether the meeting_id came from user identity or application identity.

faq.question: Can it send messages in a meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send text or approved reaction emoji when the user explicitly requests it.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: The tenant must have the right Lark application scopes, installation, data range, and VC Agent access.

faq.question: Is the bot visible to participants?
faq.answer: Yes. Joining, sending messages, and leaving are visible actions inside the meeting.
